card.title: Diffraction of light — single slit diffraction

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A single slit spreads light into a wide bright centre, with the first dark fringe at sinθ = λ/a. A narrower slit spreads the light more. A grating produces sharp maxima at d sinθ = m λ, and a single-slit minimum can wipe out a grating order.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
β = λD/d
a sinθ = mλ
r_m = √(mRλ)

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: The central maximum runs from −λ/a to +λ/a in sinθ.  ·  Missing orders sit where the single-slit factor is zero.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Diffraction is the spreading of a wave at an edge or through a narrow opening. It is obvious when the opening is comparable with the wavelength, and easy to miss when the opening is huge.  ·  A single slit of width a has a bright central band. The first dark band on either side is at sinθ = λ / a. A smaller width means a larger angle, so squeezing the slit spreads the light more.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: • Diffraction of light — single slit diffraction  ·  One slit spreads the light.  ·  The centre is bright and wide.  ·  A narrower slit makes a wider pattern.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Young's double slit: fringe width β = λD/d; 1st minimum of single slit: a sinθ = mλ.  ·  Newton's rings: r_m = √(mRλ) (dark/dark convention); λ = 2(rₙ₊₁² − rₙ²)/N (interferometric use).

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: The central band is about twice as wide as each side band, and it holds most of the light. These bands are not the equal Young's fringes. One slit does not have two coherent sources a distance d apart.  ·  Covering half the slit changes the pattern because the width a has changed. It does not simply make the old pattern dimmer with the same angles.  ·  A diffraction grating has many slits. The strong maxima satisfy d sinθ = m λ, where d is the spacing of the slits. The maxima are sharp and are used to measure wavelength.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: A grating makes sharp orders.  ·  ❌ skip the key fact → ✅ young's double slit: fringe width β = λd/d; 1st minimum of single slit: a sinθ = mλ..  ·  A narrower slit gives a wider pattern.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: The single-slit centre is bright.  ·  Do not use β = λ D / d for one slit.  ·  The grating spacing d is not the slit width a.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: a is the width of one slit.  ·  d is the distance between grating lines.  ·  Write First minimum: sinθ = λ / a and say what each symbol means.

rows.text: State the limit / condition where a formula or rule stops being valid before applying it.  ·  Limit to remember: young's double slit: fringe width β = λd/d; 1st minimum of single slit: a sinθ = mλ.  ·  The single-slit envelope still sits on top of the grating pattern. Orders that fall at a single-slit minimum are missing. That is why a grating spectrum can have a gap.
